segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Good morning. I'm Dr. Kessler. Can I start by confirming your full name and date of birth?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Sure. It's Maria Alvarez, and my date of birth is March 4th, 1988.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Thanks, Maria. And is the best number to reach you still 416-555-0182?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Yes, that's my cell.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: And you're still at 42 Maple Crescent, Apartment 3, Toronto.

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: That's right.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Great. So what brings you in today?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: My throat has been really sore for about 3 days now. It hurts a lot when I swallow, even water.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Have you had a fever?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: I think so. Last night I took my temperature and it was 38.5. I've also had chills.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Any cough, runny nose, or stuffy nose?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: No, not really. No cough at all. It's mostly just my throat, and my neck feels kind of swollen.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Has anyone around you been sick?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: My roommate, Jenna, was diagnosed with strep throat last week.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Okay, that's helpful. Have you taken anything for it?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Just Ibuprofen, 400 milligrams, maybe twice a day. It helps a little.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Any allergies to medications?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Yes, penicillin. I got hives from amoxicillin when I was a kid.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Good to know. Any other medical problems or medications you take regularly?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: No, I'm usually healthy. I don't take anything regularly.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: All right. Let me take a look. Your temperature here is 38.3, heart rate is 96, and blood pressure is 118 over 76. Open wide for me. Your tonsils are swollen and there's white exudate on both sides. The lymph nodes at the front of your neck are enlarged and tender. Your ears look normal, and your lungs are clear.

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Is that bad?

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: It fits with strep throat, with the fever, the white patches, the swollen nodes and no cough. The chance is high, so I did a rapid strep swab while we were talking. It came back positive.

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Okay, so it is strep, like Jenna?

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Yes, this is strep pharyngitis. Normally I'd give amoxicillin, but because you had hives with it, I'm going to prescribe Azithromycin instead, 500 milligrams once a day for 5 days.

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Okay. Will that clear it up quickly?

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Most people feel better within two or three days. Please finish the whole course even if you feel better. You can keep taking ibuprofen for pain and fever. Drink plenty of fluids, and warm salt water gargles can help.

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Should I stay home from work?

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Yes, stay home until you've been on the antibiotic for at least 24 hours and your fever is gone. I can give you a note for work.

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: That would be great. Thank you.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Come back or go to the emergency department if you have trouble breathing, can't swallow your own saliva, or can't open your mouth fully. And if you're not improving in 48 to 72 hours, give us a call.

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Okay, I will.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: We'll send the prescription to your pharmacy. Feel better, Maria.
